description: Reproduces staging scenario 90385279 (fixed twice): the leading option wins 89% of the time but has only a 29% modelled probability of meeting the target. The gate must catch a response that narrates the 89% win probability as the chance of hitting the goal, and must pass a response that keeps win% and target-fit distinct. Proof the gate catches the exact drift the format-analysis-for-context fix (TARGET_FIT_DEFINITION) prevents at assembly time.
user_message: Which pricing option should I go with to hit £20k MRR?

candidates.label: good
candidates.note: Keeps the two vocabularies apart: 89% is the win probability (beats the alternatives), 29% is the target-fit. Should PASS.
candidates.text: Raising prices to £59 wins most often, with an 89% win probability. That only means it beats the alternatives; it is about 29% likely to actually meet your £20k target, so leading the comparison does not guarantee the goal.

candidates.label: good_terse
candidates.note: Compound sentence carrying both numbers, each bound to its own claim (89% wins, 29% meets target). Should PASS.
candidates.text: Raising prices wins 89% of the time but is only about 29% likely to meet the £20k target.

candidates.label: regression
candidates.note: The scenario-90385279 defect: the 89% WIN probability narrated as the chance of reaching the target. Should FAIL.
candidates.text: Raising prices to £59 gives you an 89% chance of reaching your £20k target, so you are very likely to hit the goal.

candidates.label: regression_subtle
candidates.note: Same conflation without the word 'chance': the win number stated directly as target-fit. Should FAIL.
candidates.text: Raising prices to £59 is 89% likely to meet your £20k target.
